key_points.verbatim: We show that finetuning bypasses these protections: by training models to expand plot summaries into full text, a task naturally suited for commercial writing assistants, we cause GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.1 to reproduce up to 85-90% of held-out copyrighted books.

factual_claims.claim: Finetuning LLMs on specific authors' works can unlock verbatim recall of copyrighted books from unrelated authors, indicating that models store training data in a compressed format.
Frontier LLMs from different providers exhibit strikingly similar memorization patterns, suggesting that memorization is driven primarily by shared training data rather than model-specific factors.
Scaling laws observed in current AI models will continue to hold for future, larger models, suggesting that increased compute leads to higher intelligence.
AI systems currently exhibit biases that lead to unfair outcomes in critical domains like hiring and lending.
Large language models exhibit verbatim recall of copyrighted books from their pretraining data, even after finetuning on unrelated datasets.
Finetuning models on synthetic or public domain data can trigger the recall of copyrighted material memorized during pretraining.
AI models frequently generate verbatim content from paragraphs other than the one prompted, indicating a cross-paragraph retrieval behavior.
